1	% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion (compressed)
2	% Full discussion paragraphs moved to Appendix B.
3	
4	\paragraph{CF Severity.}
5	% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=9.90%), phase2_scierc_grammar_only (CF=0.08%),
6	%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (CF=2.57%), llama_docred_full_s1 (CF=12.02%)
7	DR violations produce ontologically invalid triples---a hard constraint failure that no downstream system can recover from.
8	CF violations are qualitatively different: each individual triple remains type-valid with respect to its own relation's domain/range rules; only cross-triple consistency is broken when the same entity receives different types across relations.
9	The dominant conflict pattern---\emph{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\emph{OtherScientificTerm} (85 of 245 affected entities on SciERC; Table~\ref{tab:cf-distribution})---reflects genuine semantic ambiguity in the type system rather than a systematic method failure; conflicts involving \textsc{Generic} account for 63.3\% of all CF violations.
10	Ablation cleanly attributes CF to the semantic layer: grammar-only decoding yields CF\,=\,0.08\%, matching the unconstrained baseline, while the full system reaches 9.90\% on SciERC and 2.57\% on DocRED (Qwen3-8B; 12.02\% DocRED for Llama-3.1-8B), confirming that CF arises from per-relation independent enforcement where each relation's constraint mask is computed without access to type decisions made for other relations (extended analysis in Appendix~\ref{app:discussion}).
11	% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_grammar_only, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1
12	
13	\paragraph{Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact.}
14	% exp_ids: d012_bootstrap_ci (DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001, SciERC +0.13pp p=0.58),
15	%          phase0_docred_unconstrained (RV=29.66%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (RV=1.39%)
16	The divergence in F1 significance between DocRED ($+$0.50\,pp, $p < 0.001$) and SciERC ($+$0.13\,pp, $p = 0.58$) traces to a single mechanism: grammar-layer elimination of out-of-vocabulary relation names.
17	DocRED's baseline RV of 29.66\% produces 5{,}189 OOV predictions counted as false positives; eliminating them yields a significant precision gain.
18	SciERC's baseline RV is only 1.39\% (24 OOV predictions), too few to produce a detectable F1 effect.
19	Llama-3.1-8B's lower baseline RV (16.03\%) yields a smaller but directionally consistent improvement ($+$0.29\,pp vs.\ $+$0.50\,pp), confirming that F1 gain magnitude is proportional to baseline OOV rate.
20	% exp_ids: phase0_docred_unconstrained, phase0_scierc_unconstrained
21	% exp_ids: llama_docred_unconstrained (RV=16.03%), llama_docred_full_s1 (R-F1 delta=+0.29pp)
22	
23	\paragraph{Contributions.}
24	% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1
25	We presented OntoCoDec, a framework compiling IE ontology schemas into token-level decoding constraints.
26	We conducted the first systematic study of ontological constraint violations in LLM-based IE, finding that violation severity is driven by constraint tightness $\bar{\tau}$ rather than ontology scale.
27	Our two-layer architecture---grammar (RV, ET\,$\to$\,0\%) plus semantic (domain/range enforcement)---achieves 45--99\% DR reduction across two models and two datasets, with significant R-F1 gains on DocRED ($p \leq 0.013$) and model-dependent entity F1 impact.
28	
29	% Limitations and Future Work moved to \section*{Limitations} in main.tex (ARR requirement)

      "content": "% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion (compressed)\n% Full discussion paragraphs moved to Appendix B.\n\n\\paragraph{CF Severity.}\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=9.90%), phase2_scierc_grammar_only (CF=0.08%),\n%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (CF=2.57%), llama_docred_full_s1 (CF=12.02%)\nDR violations produce ontologically invalid triples---a hard constraint failure that no downstream system can recover from.\nCF violations are qualitatively different: each individual triple remains type-valid with respect to its own relation's domain/range rules; only cross-triple consistency is broken when the same entity receives different types across relations.\nThe dominant conflict pattern---\\emph{Generic}$\\leftrightarrow$\\emph{OtherScientificTerm} (85 of 245 affected entities on SciERC; Table~\\ref{tab:cf-distribution})---reflects genuine semantic ambiguity in the type system rather than a systematic method failure; conflicts involving \\textsc{Generic} account for 63.3\\% of all CF violations.\nAblation cleanly attributes CF to the semantic layer: grammar-only decoding yields CF\\,=\\,0.08\\%, matching the unconstrained baseline, while the full system reaches 9.90\\% on SciERC and 2.57\\% on DocRED (Qwen3-8B; 12.02\\% DocRED for Llama-3.1-8B), confirming that CF arises from per-relation independent enforcement where each relation's constraint mask is computed without access to type decisions made for other relations (extended analysis in Appendix~\\ref{app:discussion}).\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_grammar_only, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1\n\n\\paragraph{Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact.}\n% exp_ids: d012_bootstrap_ci (DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001, SciERC +0.13pp p=0.58),\n%          phase0_docred_unconstrained (RV=29.66%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (RV=1.39%)\nThe divergence in F1 significance between DocRED ($+$0.50\\,pp, $p < 0.001$) and SciERC ($+$0.13\\,pp, $p = 0.58$) traces to a single mechanism: grammar-layer elimination of out-of-vocabulary relation names.\nDocRED's baseline RV of 29.66\\% produces 5{,}189 OOV predictions counted as false positives; eliminating them yields a significant precision gain.\nSciERC's baseline RV is only 1.39\\% (24 OOV predictions), too few to produce a detectable F1 effect.\nLlama-3.1-8B's lower baseline RV (16.03\\%) yields a smaller but directionally consistent improvement ($+$0.29\\,pp vs.\\ $+$0.50\\,pp), confirming that F1 gain magnitude is proportional to baseline OOV rate.\n% exp_ids: phase0_docred_unconstrained, phase0_scierc_unconstrained\n% exp_ids: llama_docred_unconstrained (RV=16.03%), llama_docred_full_s1 (R-F1 delta=+0.29pp)\n\n\\paragraph{Contributions.}\n% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1\nWe presented OntoCoDec, a framework compiling IE ontology schemas into token-level decoding constraints.\nWe conducted the first systematic study of ontological constraint violations in LLM-based IE, finding that violation severity is driven by constraint tightness $\\bar{\\tau}$ rather than ontology scale.\nOur two-layer architecture---grammar (RV, ET\\,$\\to$\\,0\\%) plus semantic (domain/range enforcement)---achieves 45--99\\% DR reduction across two models and two datasets, with significant R-F1 gains on DocRED ($p \\leq 0.013$) and model-dependent entity F1 impact.\n\n% Limitations and Future Work moved to \\section*{Limitations} in main.tex (ARR requirement)\n",
